paraphrase: In a past life as the captain Great Compassionate, the Buddha, knowing that a robber on the ship intended to kill five hundred merchants (bodhisattvas), killed him out of compassion — to save the merchants and to spare the robber the hell-karma of the deed — accepting the karmic consequence himself; this is presented as skillful means.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. Stated as narrative of an exceptional bodhisattva act; the same sūtra says such acts are not for ordinary practitioners (from memory).
